# ethereum-optimism/optimism Daily Update (Jun 11, 2026)
## OVERVIEW 
Today's development focused on enhancing contract validation, refining fee calculations, and improving node operator documentation, alongside significant updates to the op-reth client and various maintenance tasks.

## KEY TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENTS

### Core Protocol Enhancements & Fee Logic
Significant progress was made in validating L2 chain IDs within the `OPContractsManagerMigrator` to prevent duplicates and ensure consistency across the Superchain [#20926]. A new `op-core/fees` package was introduced to centralize L1 data-availability cost and operator-fee calculations, improving modularity and accuracy [#21314].

### Node Client Improvements & Configuration
The `op-reth` client now supports a configurable maximum uncompressed block size, addressing potential issues with consensus-layer clients that have size limits [#21353]. Additionally, the `op-reth` client was updated to v2.3.0, incorporating 158 upstream commits and syncing shared dependencies across workspaces [#21348]. Support for `getPayloadV5` was added for the Osaka (Karst) hardfork, ensuring compatibility with the latest engine API [#21337].

### Documentation and AI Tooling Updates
Several documentation updates were made for node operators, defaulting guides to `op-reth` and providing comprehensive information on configuration and management [#21037], [#21057]. New AI-related documentation was added, including `devfeatures.md` and guidance for Rust pre-commit ordering, to improve agent tooling and development workflows [#21350]. A new `dispute-game-investigator` skill and guide were also added to assist in diagnosing fault dispute games [#21333].

## NEWLY OPENED PULL REQUESTS
- [#21356](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21356) op-core/types: add DepositTx, PostExecTx and Receipt types
- [#21351](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21351) feat(op-chain-ops): promote op-up interop smoke tests to standalone interop-smoke tool
- [#21349](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21349) feat(op-chain-ops): promote op-up interop smoke tests to standalone interop-smoke tool
- [#21347](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21347) perf(kona-driver): decode only the L1-info deposit when computing L2BlockInfo
- [#21346](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21346) refactor(contracts): track predeploy initialization in registry
- [#21345](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21345) feat(op-chain-ops): validate L2 genesis allocs in production generation
- [#21343](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21343) fix(contracts): clear residual proxy admin owner nonce in L2 genesis

## CLOSED ISSUES

### Deprecation and Removal of Legacy Components
Several issues related to the `op-program` and `op-geth` were closed due to their deprecation and removal. This includes switching CI jobs from `op-program` to `kona-proof` [#19789], rebuilding `op-program` prestate [#17867], and fixing `vm-compat` for `go1.25` in `op-program` [#18334]. The `op-validator` tool was also removed as it was unused and configuration validation is now handled elsewhere [#21308].

### Fee Calculation and Contract Validation Improvements
Issues concerning budget handling in `txinclude` for U17 and U18 were resolved with the introduction of the `op-core/fees` package [#17817], [#20261]. A critical fix was implemented to prevent the `OPContractsManagerMigrator` from accepting duplicate chain IDs, enhancing contract security [#20882].

### Node Operator Tooling and Documentation
Improvements were made to node operator tooling and documentation. This includes ensuring interop filter RPC nodes support appropriate pruning configurations [#21190] and updating `op-reth` fork activation helpers to correctly include L1 (Ethereum) forks [#21239]. Support for `PostExec` transactions in `kona-node` was also implemented, making the Rust rollup node SDM-ready [#21185].

### Developer Experience and CI/CD Enhancements
Several issues related to developer experience and CI/CD were closed. This includes addressing compiler errors caused by monorepo dependency updates [#424], improving Ledger device connection checks before running tasks [#417], and enhancing CI checks for domain hash and message validation [#717]. Updates were also made to documentation regarding two-step simulation links [#789] and the `just sign-stack` command now validates the selected signer against the target Safe [#1295].

## NEW ISSUES

### L2 Genesis Configuration and Validation
New issues have been opened to enhance the L2 genesis process. This includes clearing residual proxy admin owner nonces [#21339], validating L2 genesis allocations against expected accounts [#21340], and refactoring the Predeploy Registry to track initialization properties [#21341]. A new `deploy(FullConfig)` function is also proposed for `L2ContractsManager` to streamline L2 genesis deployment [#21342].

### SDM and Rollup Builder Discrepancies
A critical issue was identified where `op-rbuilder`'s published SDM post-exec payload diverges from `op-node`'s derived one with the Osaka L1 fork active, leading to test failures [#21354]. This highlights a need for increased coverage in `rust/kona/tests/proofs` for SDM [#21344].

## ACTIVE ISSUES

### `CANNON_KONA` Feature Flag Removal [#20249]
The discussion revolves around the removal of the `CANNON_KONA` feature flag. @Inphi commented that the audit is complete, suggesting the flag can now be removed. This indicates progress towards simplifying the codebase and removing temporary feature flags.

### Normalized Hashing in `AccountAccessParser` [#1064]
@mds1 closed this issue as stale, noting that the normalized state diff hash code it referred to was removed in a previous PR. This indicates that the original problem has been addressed through a different architectural change.

### `DisputeGameUpgrade`: Moving Post- to Pre-checks [#444]
@mds1 closed this issue as stale, stating that it targeted an old `DisputeGameUpgrade` flow which has since been removed. This suggests that the proposed refactoring is no longer relevant due to changes in the dispute game architecture.
